score.doctor_diagnosis: Clostridioides difficile infection (antibiotic-associated pseudomembranous colitis) secondary to levofloxacin therapy — non-severe/hospital-acquired.
score.doctor_final_text:
Everything points one way: fluoroquinolone exposure in hospital, nine watery stools a day, tenderness and leukocytosis. I'll stop levofloxacin if your pneumonia allows, start oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily for 10 days, keep you on contact precautions, and avoid anti-motility agents while we await the toxin assay.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (antibiotic-associated pseudomembranous colitis) secondary to levofloxacin therapy — non-severe/hospital-acquired.

dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent — I understand you've been having diarrhea recently. When did it start, and how many loose stools are you having each day?
It started about two days ago, and I've had at least 9 episodes of watery diarrhea since then. It's been pretty frequent and uncomfortable.
Any blood or mucus in the stool, and have you had fever, vomiting, or severe abdominal cramping?
No, I haven't seen any blood or mucus in the stool, and I haven't had any fever or vomiting. I do have some lower abdominal cramping and discomfort though, especially with the diarrhea episodes.
Have you taken any antibiotics recently, or been in a hospital or care facility in the past couple of months?
Yes, I've been on levofloxacin for a few days now for pneumonia treatment here on the medical floor. That's the only antibiotic I've been taking recently.

That combination — antibiotics on a hospital floor plus frequent watery stools — makes me think of *C. difficile*; let me check your stool and labs.

Your white count is up at 13,400 with 80% neutrophils, which fits an inflammatory colitis. While the C. diff assay finishes — are you also taking any acid-suppressing medication like a proton pump inhibitor, and has your abdomen become distended or tender to touch?
No, I'm not taking any acid-suppressing medications like that. My abdomen does feel a bit tender, especially in the lower part when I press on it, but I wouldn't say it's really distended or bloated.
Good — no distension makes fulminant colitis unlikely. Has anyone else on the floor or in your family had similar diarrhea, and are you able to keep fluids down?
No, I haven't heard of anyone else on the floor having this problem, and no one in my family has been sick like this either. I am able to drink fluids and keep them down without any trouble.

Good — you're hydrating well, which is reassuring. Let me get the pending toxin result and check your colon for wall thickening.
